access.edition_or_version: English translation by Ivan Morris (Alfred A. Knopf, 1957)

mechanics.premise: A sick, starving Imperial Japanese soldier wanders the Philippines during the final months of the Second World War, sliding toward madness and atrocity among other stragglers.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person; a mind losing its claim on social and moral order.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Clinical attention to bodily decay, hunger, and horror; matter-of-fact register applied to cannibalism and death; religious imagery hollowed out rather than consoling.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Hunger and shame -> isolation -> moral collapse -> ambiguous survival without redemption.
mechanics.dialogue: Sparse and wary; language itself erodes as the protagonist's world contracts.
mechanics.setting: A Philippine island stripped of order; jungle and plain as a place of dying.
mechanics.critical_reception: Won the Yomiuri Prize; adapted to film in 1959 and 2014. Cited as a non-Anglophone instance of unflinching war bleakness.
mechanics.verification_note: Existence, 1951 date, Yomiuri Prize, and premise confirmed via Wikipedia 'Fires on the Plain (novel)' API extract. No text reproduced. Translation limits: Japanese registers of shame and military duty are only partly carried by English.
